query: In Experiment 4, the same 24 observers that participated in Experiment 2 performed two consecutive tasks on each trial. First, they were simultaneously presented with two Gabor stimuli and were cued to reproduce the orientation of one of the stimuli by adjusting a response bar. We termed the cued stimulus 'inducer', since it induced a perceptual decision at one location. In order to measure subsequent biases in perception, another two Gabor stimuli were presented (one at the previously cued location and one at a location in the opposite hemifield, 20 visual degrees apart) and observers judged which of the two stimuli was tilted more clockwise (two-alternative forced choice [2AFC], Figure 5A and B).
